title: Interrupted knowledge work: resume a real task without losing context
problem_statement: Knowledge workers and agent builders can lose the thread of a real task after interruptions. Brali should be tested on whether its existing trusted problem-to-protocol path helps a person or an external integration recover a concrete next action without hiding uncertainty, provenance or failure.
hypothesis: For interrupted knowledge work, Brali can help a meaningful share of real human trials reach a concrete next action and can help external agent integrations retrieve a bounded trusted packet while preserving evidence and provenance. The scenario remains unvalidated until real reviewed evidence exists.

procedure: Use a participant's own recent interrupted knowledge-work task. Do not collect the task text, employer/client material, names, account identifiers or other personal data into the repository.

Before using Brali, record only a privacy-safe categorical description of the current workaround and whether the person already has a concrete next action. Do not treat interest or compliments as outcome evidence.
Use the current public Brali path: Ask Brali for a trusted match or explicit no-answer, inspect the bounded recommendation, then use the Protocol Runner when a trusted protocol is available.

After the attempt, record whether a concrete next action was reached, whether the protocol was started/completed, explicit helpful/not-helpful feedback, abandonment or workaround, and any rejected alternative. Reuse existing privacy-light outcome events whenever they represent the observation.
Record repeat use only after a separate later real attempt is deliberately reported. Do not infer return usage from page views, cookies, local storage, downloads or repository activity.
success_criteria: At least 10 real human attempts are reviewed before a keep/change/reject decision is made.
At least 6 reviewed human attempts reach a concrete next action that was not already present before Brali, with the observation linked to a privacy-safe source reference.
At least 5 reviewed human attempts contain both a protocol-completed signal and explicit helpful feedback for the same real attempt; generated demos and fixtures do not count.
At least 3 later real attempts are explicitly reported as repeat use or reuse of a Brali protocol; repeat use is never inferred from traffic or anonymous page opens.
Negative outcomes, abandonment, workarounds and rejected alternatives are retained under the same review rules as positive outcomes.
failure_criteria: After at least 10 reviewed attempts, fewer than 4 reach a concrete next action attributable to the Brali interaction rather than a pre-existing plan.
Trust, safety, fit or clarity failures repeatedly cause abandonment in at least 4 reviewed attempts.
The experiment cannot distinguish a real protocol attempt/completion from page exposure without collecting data outside the declared privacy boundary.

procedure: Run each attempt from a clean external integration context using only public Brali interfaces available at the time of the attempt. Record the exact interface and version; do not describe repository-ready source as a hosted service.
Test a realistic interrupted-work query through the maintained trusted retrieval path. A correct explicit no-answer is a valid result when Brali lacks eligible coverage.
Verify that canonical Brali IDs/URLs, locale availability where exposed, evidence state, limitations and provenance survive the integration boundary.

Record setup friction, malformed or missing metadata, trust-boundary failures, correct no-answer behavior, and whether the integration can repeat the retrieval without a repository-specific hidden workaround.

Use privacy-light integration outcome events where they fit. Provider-visible artifacts may be referenced for transport/discovery verification, but CI or source existence alone is not an external observation.
success_criteria: All 5 planned external integration attempts are actually attempted before a keep/change/reject decision is made for this track.
At least 4 reviewed attempts return either an eligible trusted packet or the correct explicit no-answer without leaking pending-review or restricted material as a recommendation.
At least 4 reviewed attempts preserve canonical identity, evidence state and provenance across the integration boundary.
At least 3 reviewed attempts can repeat the retrieval from the documented public integration path without repository checkout-specific assumptions beyond those explicitly required by that interface.
failure_criteria: Two or more reviewed attempts lose evidence/provenance or expose review-gated material as trusted guidance.
Three or more reviewed attempts require undocumented repository-specific workarounds to reach the maintained integration path.
The integration path fabricates an answer when trusted coverage is insufficient instead of returning explicit no-answer semantics.

limitations: No real human or external integration attempt has yet been accepted into this experiment registry.
Targets and thresholds are pre-registered experiment criteria, not adoption, usefulness or conversion claims.
The current outcome registry is privacy-light and deliberately does not identify people across sessions; repeat use therefore requires a separate explicit report rather than passive tracking.

privacy.observation_reference_policy: Store only privacy-safe references needed to audit an accepted observation: canonical Brali IDs, accepted outcome event IDs, public GitHub issue references, provider-visible artifacts or a maintainer review reference. Never store raw task/prompt text, employer/client material, names, contact details or persistent person identifiers in this registry.
